decisionsTitle: The outbox paces Mailgun to an hourly allowance, and a rate refusal is a pause, never a loss (amending §100 and §163)
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-01, forwarding Mailgun's notice:** «Urgent! Am primit asta de la Mailgun!» The notice read: «You are sending too fast. Your account is on probation and domains are limited to 100 messages / hour. To maintain the rate the account has been temporarily disabled. The account will be enabled in 847 seconds.» Why the account was on probation is not said, and this record does not guess.

**The day.** The club opened registrations: the morning a race's confirmations, declaration requests and the club's copies all leave at once, against a domain limited to a hundred an hour.

**What the code did.** Nothing paced Mailgun: the outbox sent as fast as the queue filled — twenty a batch from the job, twenty from every request's drain under «imediat», forty from every «Trimite acum». A **429** was a transient failure (§40: "the hourly rate limit, which clears within the hour"), so it got the ordinary backoff — one, two, four, eight, sixteen, thirty-two minutes — and after the sixth attempt, about an hour, the message was **FAILED**: a runner's confirmation lost, and the account knocked on six more times while Mailgun was asking it to stop. The status the API returns for the probation was not observed: the notice is an email. If it is a **400** "… is not allowed to send: … temporarily disabled" (the shape §40 describes for Mailgun's disabled domains, anticipated, not seen), it matched no limit language (`ALLOWANCE_SPENT`, §40), so it was **permanent** — BOUNCED, never tried again. Nothing in the plan setting (§100) knew an hourly figure existed.

**Decision — A, the pace.** The email plan setting gains `hourlyAllowance` (1–100 000, or empty), **100 when the stored value has none**, so production paces from the first deploy without anybody touching it. An Administrator sets it on «Setări» → «Emailuri» → «Limita pe oră», with one line of help and the probation behind its «?», in both languages; the audit row `email_plan.changed` names it from and to, like the plan's ceilings. Before claiming Mailgun's road, `claimOutboxBatch` takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock (two workers claiming at once, READ COMMITTED, would otherwise read the same room and together go over the hour: the second waits the milliseconds the first needs, and its count sees the first's rows as in flight), then counts in one query what Mailgun carried in the trailing sixty-one minutes (`sent_at` inside the window — a minute of margin, below — every road but Gmail's, captured messages excluded — they never reached Mailgun — each row as its `recipient_count`, since Mailgun bills every recipient, a copy included, as a message; a null count is one) and what another worker holds for it right now, one row each, and claims at most `hourlyAllowance − that`, oldest first — nothing at all from Mailgun's road while a pause Mailgun asked for is not over (B). What is not claimed is not touched: no `next_attempt_at` is written, and the next drain or job run (every fifteen minutes by day) takes it when the hour has room. Gmail's road is not held to it. The after-response drain and «Trimite acum» go through the same claim; a press the hour has no room for is refused with its own sentence unless a Gmail-road message is due, which the pace does not hold (`SEND_NOW_HOUR_SPENT`: «Alege «Pune la coadă»; emailul pleacă singur când ora are din nou loc.»), exactly as the day's allowance refuses (§80, §540). `/admin/emails` says «Trimise în ultima oră: N din 100» beside the day's count. `/api/health` counts Mailgun-road rows held for the hour as `hourPaced`, not `overdue`, while the hour binds — Mailgun's road carried a full allowance in the last ninety minutes, or is carrying the rest of it now — the same judgement the queue panel's red «late» makes, each row knowing its road (§529).

**Decision — B, the refusals.** `classifyMailgunFailure(status, body, headers)` — the adapter now hands it the response's headers. A **429** is a **pause**: throttled, `paced`, due again at Mailgun's `Retry-After` (seconds or an HTTP date; never in the past, never more than a day), or in fifteen minutes without one. A **400** whose body says "not allowed to send" *together with* temporarily, account disabled, probation, too fast or rate limit is the same pause, fifteen minutes; a bare "domain disabled" stays permanent (a domain Mailgun closed for good would otherwise retry forever; the trade-off is that a permanent closure worded "account disabled" is paused, and only the paused-row overdue rule flags it). The outbox gives the attempt back on a pause — a pause is not a refusal of the message, so no number of pauses spends the six attempts — keeps the reason on the row, and holds the rest of the batch's Mailgun messages until the same instant instead of knocking again at once — without the reason, which stays on the row Mailgun refused, so batch-mates waiting for the pace are never read as paused by `/api/health`. The marked row then holds Mailgun's whole road: while it waits for a pause not yet over, the claim takes no Mailgun row at all, so no later drain sends into the same refusal. A message Mailgun paused recently (its pause ended, or ends, within ninety minutes) and queued longer ago than the overdue allowance is `overdue` on `/api/health`, pace or no pace: a pause that never ends needs a person, and `lastError` says which refusal.

**Why 100 by default.** The probation is in force now, and a stored value from before the field must pace from the first deploy. 100 is Mailgun's limit itself, with no margin beyond the window's extra minute and the send's own timestamp, so `SETUP.md` §35 and the box's help ask for 90 while the probation lasts. QA defaults to 100 too and shares the domain, so together they could send 200 in Mailgun's hour: `SETUP.md` §35 asks to set QA's «Limita pe oră» to about 10 now (the owner decides). A pace that is too low costs minutes — the queue leaves a little later, and nothing is lost; one that is too high costs the account, disabled on registration morning. Once Mailgun's support lifts the probation, the Administrator raises the figure or clears it (`SETUP.md` §35).

**Kept.** Nothing is lost: an unclaimed row waits untouched, a paused one waits with its attempt. The daily deferral is unchanged — 402, 420 and a 400 with limit language still go to the reset (§40, §100). The 400s §40 keeps permanent stay permanent: the sandbox's «Sandbox subdomains are for test purposes only» and its unauthorized recipient, an unverified domain, a malformed message; 401 and 403 stay permanent. Gmail's road, its cap and its pace are unaffected (§443). The plan catalogue is unchanged: no plan row carries an hourly figure.

**What it does not cover.** Each environment counts only its own outbox, and QA sends through the same domain (§307): a QA rehearsal's messages come off production's hour at Mailgun without production knowing. `SETUP.md` §35 says to keep rehearsals small during the probation, or set QA's box lower. A Gmail-road message that falls back to Mailgun after a Gmail failure is not counted before it leaves; if it tips the hour over, Mailgun's 429 pauses it.

**Tests.** Unit `notifications/mailgun-classification.test.ts`: a 429 with `Retry-After: 847`, with an HTTP date, without one, with an unreadable or absurd one; the probation's 400 paused; the sandbox's 400 with "not allowed to send" and a bare "domain disabled" still permanent; every earlier case unchanged. Unit `notifications/mailgun-adapter.test.ts`: the response's `Retry-After` reaches the classifier. Unit `notifications/email-plan.test.ts`: the default of 100 from an old value, a cleared box, the bounds, no catalogue row with an hourly figure, the room arithmetic, the hour that binds only at a full allowance, the sixty-one-minute window and a pause recent only within ninety minutes. Integration `notifications/hourly-pace.test.ts` (PGlite): 100 sent in the last hour → no Mailgun row claimed and Gmail's as before; 60 → 40, oldest first, Gmail's sends not counted; 100 sent sixty and a half minutes ago → none (the margin), a minute later a full batch; a Mailgun send stamped when the call returned, not at the batch's start; a two-recipient row counts two and a row in flight one; another worker's batch counted; a pause hands the batch back with its attempts and is not claimed early; a pause holds Mailgun's whole road — a fresh due row is not claimed a minute later, Gmail's road is — and both go once it ends; twelve pauses never FAIL a message; «Trimite acum» and a resend's «now» refused with the hour's sentence, and a press with Gmail rows due sends them while Mailgun's hour is spent; health's `hourPaced` only while the hour binds and only on Mailgun's road, a recently paused row that turns overdue and an old pause mark judged as any waiting row; the setting's default, round trip and audit row; the page's figure and whether the hour binds; unit `notifications/outbox-queue-panel.test.ts`: the panel's «late» by the same rules; batch-mates released without the pause mark; a recipient count of 3 spends 3 of the hour. Concurrency `tests/concurrency/hourly-pace.test.ts` (real PostgreSQL, two connections and more): four workers claiming at once never take more than the hour's room.

**After review (2026-10-01).** Four things tightened. *The pause holds the road:* it held only the batch it happened in, so under «imediat» every registration's after-response drain would have claimed the next due Mailgun row and sent it into the same refusal during the 847 seconds — the knocking that keeps an account on probation disabled. The claim now takes nothing from Mailgun's road while any waiting Mailgun row carries the pause mark with its pause not over: one more conditional count in the same query, under the same advisory lock. *The hour has a margin:* a Mailgun send's `sent_at` was the batch's start, so a batch's last sends looked older than they were and left the window early; it is now the moment the call returned, on the batch's own clock (`now` moved on by the real time elapsed). The window is sixty-one minutes, because our clock and Mailgun's are not one clock; sent rows count in recipients, rows in flight one each. *Health counts the hour only when it binds,* and only on Mailgun's road: a Gmail row, or a Mailgun row behind an hour with room, is overdue as before the pace; a rate-paused row whose pause is older than ninety minutes is waiting its turn and judged as any waiting row. The trade-off: a backlog that the batch size holds back rather than the hour — twenty a run on the hourly night pinger, under a hundred an hour — now reads overdue rather than paced; the queue is slower than its inflow there, and that is worth a person's look. *«Trimite acum» with only Gmail's rows due* already went through while Mailgun's hour was spent; a test now holds it there.

**Amends** §100 (the setting gains a field that is not a plan's), §40 (a 429 was transient, a "not allowed to send" 400 without limit language permanent) and §163 (a QA that may address anyone, through the club's domain since §307, now also spends the domain's hour).

*Rejected:* slowing the job's cadence — the after-response drain and «Trimite acum» would still burst a hundred in a minute; a cap in the Mailgun plan catalogue — the probation is the account's, not the plan's, and it ends when support lifts it; treating every 400 as a pause — a bad address, the sandbox's refusal or an unverified domain must stay permanent, or the outbox retries a hopeless message forever.
changelogLine: - **Mailgun's hourly limit is respected** — the outbox sends at most the hour's allowance (100 by default, set on «Emailuri»; 90 is advised during Mailgun's probation), stops Mailgun's road while Mailgun asks it to wait and pauses on a rate refusal instead of giving up, so an account on probation is not knocked on again and no confirmation email is lost. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given the email plan's «Limita pe oră» (100 when never set; empty is no pace), when the outbox claims a batch — the job, the drain after a response or «Trimite acum» — then Mailgun's road takes at most the allowance less what Mailgun carried in the trailing sixty-one minutes, in recipients, and the rows another worker holds, one each, oldest first; a Mailgun send is stamped when the provider took it, not at its batch's start; Gmail's road is not held to it; an unclaimed row keeps its turn and attempts; a «now» press the hour has no room for is refused with its own sentence unless a Gmail-road message is due, which it then sends; two workers claiming at once never go over the hour (an advisory lock); `/admin/emails` shows «Trimise în ultima oră: N din …»; and `/api/health` and the queue panel count late Mailgun-road rows as `hourPaced`, not overdue, only while Mailgun's road carried a full allowance in the last ninety minutes or is carrying the rest of it now (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given Mailgun answers a send with a 429, or a 400 saying it is not allowed to send because the account is temporarily stopped, disabled, on probation, too fast or rate limited, when the outbox records it, then the message is PENDING again at Mailgun's `Retry-After` (seconds or an HTTP date) or fifteen minutes later, its attempt given back so no number of pauses marks it FAILED, it alone carries the pause mark, and until the pause ends no Mailgun row is claimed — the batch's others nor any later one — while Gmail's road still is; a row paused within the last ninety minutes and queued longer ago than the overdue allowance is overdue on `/api/health` and late on the queue panel, and an older pause mark is judged as any waiting row; the sandbox's and an unverified domain's 400s, 401 and 403 stay permanent, and the daily allowance's refusals still wait for the reset (2026-10-01, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the outbox paces Mailgun to 100 an hour; a rate refusal is a pause
